The incident happened towards the end of US rapper Don Toliver's show at the Co-op Live arena at about 22:00. The North West Ambulance Service said one person was taken to hospital for further assessment while more than 50 people were assessed for "eye and respiratory symptoms". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a major incident was declared after reports of people suffering from the effects of an unknown substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas. Footage on social media showed emergency services converge on the arena, while some concertgoers were seen coughing as they streamed out of the venue. In a statement early on Monday, GMP said more than 12,000 people had been safely evacuated, with several people assessed for side effects. "Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert," GMP Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said. "Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital. evidence_packet.title: ITV investigating Coronation Street actor Jacob Roberts after bar incident

evidence_packet.evidence_text: ITV investigating Coronation Street actor Jacob Roberts after bar incident - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jacob Roberts has starred in Coronation Street since 2024 By Miriam Barker North West Published 22 November 2026 ITV is investigating a Coronation Street actor following an alleged bar altercation. Jacob Roberts is known for playing Det Con Kit Green on the ITV soap since 2024. According to reports by the Sun newspaper, video footage appears to show him shouting outside Kiely's Irish Bar in Manchester on 8 November. Greater Manchester Police said officers had attended a bar in Watson Street at about 02:30 GMT following reports of a disturbance. No arrests have been made. An ITV spokesperson said they were investigating and would be speaking with Roberts. Roberts was allegedly trying to get into the bar, with staff claiming he was acting aggressively and swearing when he was told he could not come in as the venue was closing. Roberts previously played Damon Kinsella on the Channel 4 soap Hollyoaks from 2017 until 2023, before joining the cobbles in 2024. He has also appeared in Emmerdale and recently starred in the crossover episode Corridale. His storylines on Coronation Street include being diagnosed with male breast cancer as well as fathering a child after an illicit affair with his girlfriend's daughter. Roberts' representatives have been contacted for comment. title: Murdered teen's legacy inspired my law career, trainee barrister says

evidence_packet.title: Murdered teen's legacy inspired my law career, trainee barrister says
evidence_packet.lead: Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester says the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme has given her confidence
evidence_packet.summary: Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester says the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme has given her confidence
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who has been supported to train as a barrister by a bursary which honours a murdered teenager has said she wants to become a "hard-working" prosecutor who "treats witnesses with care" Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester, said being chosen for the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme, which supports aspiring lawyers from under-represented backgrounds, had given her the confidence to "reach my goals" and "opened doors" The bursary is a tribute to 18-year-old Anthony, who had ambitions to study law but was murdered in a racist attack on Merseyside in 2005 Uche said she had been inspired by his family's fight for justice and wanted to draw on Anthony's own values when building her career Anthony's mother, Dr Gee Walker, set up a foundation in her son's name to tackle racism, hate crime and discrimination In partnership with the CPS and the National Black Crown Prosecution Association, the foundation offers an Anthony Walker Bursary - as well as a mentor - to help aspiring lawyers from under-represented Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds in the north-west of England

Jungle Junction in Denton, Greater Manchester, was temporarily closed in October by Ofsted and given a list of steps it needed to take in order to reopen. It included an order that "food is prepared in a way that prevents choking and children are within sight and hearing of staff". Denton Daycare Ltd later decided to permanently close, citing the company's "financial challenges". The watchdog report revealed inspectors also told the nursery to ensure proper hand washing routines were implemented, install better safeguarding procedures and give all children daily access to outdoor play. Arrangements for children with special educational needs and disabilities were also criticised. Denton Daycare Ltd company director Alina Naveed apologised to parents for the "difficult circumstances" they are facing having to find alternative childcare at such short notice - as well as staff. Keeley's three-year-old son was one of the nursery's children and she told the Local Democracy Reporting Service reading the Ofsted letter "left me feeling quite shocked" at the "sheer number and seriousness of the failures identified". "You expect [your child] to be safe, cared for and supported, and some of the things highlighted in that letter are really difficult to read," she added. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Colin and Carol Hill's love story began on the dance floor more than 70 years ago. Now in their nineties, they still play table tennis and attend keep-fit classes, and say staying active has helped keep their romance alive Colin, 91, and Carol, 90, from Cleveleys, married two years after meeting at the historic Hill Stores Ballroom in Oldham in 1954 Colin walked Carol home after their first dance and declared he was going to marry her. Her response was simple: "No way." However, Colin won her over and, more than seven decades later, the couple say they are as much in love now as they were as newlyweds Reflecting on their platinum anniversary, husband Colin said he felt "blessed" to have had Carol by his side He said the secret to their marriage was "respecting each other", and added that his wife still looked "a million dollars"

evidence_packet.lead: A row over changes to planning rules has left a Greater Manchester council unable to make planning decisions, including in Angela Rayner's constituency The Housing Secretary's department has introduced reforms intended to speed up housebuilding by allowing officers to sign off sm
evidence_packet.summary: A row over changes to planning rules has left a Greater Manchester council unable to make planning decisions, including in Angela Rayner's constituency The Housing Secretary's department has introduced reforms intended to speed up housebuilding by allowing officers to sign off sm
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A row over changes to planning rules has left a Greater Manchester council unable to make planning decisions, including in Angela Rayner's constituency The Housing Secretary's department has introduced reforms intended to speed up housebuilding by allowing officers to sign off smaller schemes without councillor involvement In Tameside, which is a Labour-led minority administration, opposition councillors have refused to adopt the changes at successive meetings Subsequently, the authority said that "no planning decisions or determinations are currently being made." Councillors will still have a say on larger developments, which will continue to go before planning committees. However, smaller and more technical applications would only be dealt with by planning officers Reform UK is the second largest party in Tameside. Its group leader, councillor Allan Hopwood, has vowed to continue fighting the changes

title: Murdered teen's legacy inspired my law career, trainee barrister says

evidence_packet.title: Murdered teen's legacy inspired my law career, trainee barrister says
evidence_packet.lead: A woman who has been supported to train as a barrister by a bursary which honours a murdered teenager has said she wants to become a "hard-working" prosecutor who "treats witnesses with care" Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester, said being chosen for the Anthony Walker Bursary Schem
evidence_packet.summary: A woman who has been supported to train as a barrister by a bursary which honours a murdered teenager has said she wants to become a "hard-working" prosecutor who "treats witnesses with care" Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester, said being chosen for the Anthony Walker Bursary Schem
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who has been supported to train as a barrister by a bursary which honours a murdered teenager has said she wants to become a "hard-working" prosecutor who "treats witnesses with care" Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester, said being chosen for the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme, which supports aspiring lawyers from under-represented backgrounds, had given her the confidence to "reach my goals" and "opened doors" The bursary is a tribute to 18-year-old Anthony, who had ambitions to study law but was murdered in a racist attack on Merseyside in 2005 Uche said she had been inspired by his family's fight for justice and wanted to draw on Anthony's own values when building her career Anthony's mother, Dr Gee Walker, set up a foundation in her son's name to tackle racism, hate crime and discrimination In partnership with the CPS and the National Black Crown Prosecution Association, the foundation offers an Anthony Walker Bursary - as well as a mentor - to help aspiring lawyers from under-represented Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds in the north-west of England

evidence_packet.summary: Parents whose children went to a nursery that was shut down last month due to a "risk to children's safety" reacted as a report revealed the extent of inspectors' concerns Jungle Junction in Denton, Greater Manchester, was temporarily closed in October by Ofsted and given a list
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Parents whose children went to a nursery that was shut down last month due to a "risk to children's safety" reacted as a report revealed the extent of inspectors' concerns Jungle Junction in Denton, Greater Manchester, was temporarily closed in October by Ofsted and given a list of steps it needed to take in order to reopen It included an order that "food is prepared in a way that prevents choking and children are within sight and hearing of staff" Denton Daycare Ltd later decided to permanently close, citing the company's "financial challenges" The watchdog report revealed inspectors also told the nursery to ensure proper hand washing routines were implemented, install better safeguarding procedures and give all children daily access to outdoor play Arrangements for children with special educational needs and disabilities were also criticised

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Colin and Carol Hill's love story began on the dance floor more than 70 years ago. Now in their nineties, they still play table tennis and attend keep-fit classes, and say staying active has helped keep their romance alive Colin, 91, and Carol, 90, from Cleveleys, married two years after meeting at the historic Hill Stores Ballroom in Oldham in 1954 Colin walked Carol home after their first dance and declared he was going to marry her. Her response was simple: "No way." However, Colin won her over and, more than seven decades later, the couple say they are as much in love now as they were as newlyweds Reflecting on their platinum anniversary, husband Colin said he felt "blessed" to have had Carol by his side He said the secret to their marriage was "respecting each other", and added that his wife still looked "a million dollars"

evidence_packet.summary: The mother of a 16-year-old boy who was stabbed to death and later campaigned to provide bleed-control kits for communities said she was "overwhelmed" as the 100th piece of life-saving equipment was unveiled Rhamero West was murdered in Old Trafford, Manchester, in September 2021
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mother of a 16-year-old boy who was stabbed to death and later campaigned to provide bleed-control kits for communities said she was "overwhelmed" as the 100th piece of life-saving equipment was unveiled Rhamero West was murdered in Old Trafford, Manchester, in September 2021 after a car chase in the city. Another shouted "What the f*** was that smell bro? I can't breathe bro. Bro what was that?!" Molly, a 22-year-old fan who made her way from Derbyshire for the gig, had a bird’s eye view of the incident on the balcony. Scene inside Co-op live during Don Toliver gig . . . . Concertgoers at Co-op Live in Manchester were evacuated on Sunday night (November 22), during Don Toliver’s NITROUS show. Emergency services and police attended the scene and a cordon was put in place outside the venue.. Eyewitnesses said the standing area was cleared at around 10pm, shortly after Don Toliver finished performing on the B stage.. Greater Manchester Police said an 'unknown substance' - reported to be tear gas - was released into the crowd towards the end of the concert.. Over 12,000 fans in attendance were evacuated immediately.. A major incident was declared by police, with one fan in hospital.. Over 50 people fell ill and were medically assessed, paramedics said.. A video that captured the moment officials formally stopped the event shows a staff member telling the audience the show was finished and asked people to leave via the nearest exit.. GMP said those showing signs of being affected were being supported by emergency services. Police added that no serious injuries had been reported but one person was in hospital.. Police asked people to stay away from the arena while emergency services managed the evacuation and helped concertgoers get to transport home.. In a statement, Co-op Live said it will work with police to identify what happened and 'appropriate action' to be taken.. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport’s Senior Coroner Alison Mutch has warned of her concerns that the continued heading of the ball by footballers could lead to death The warning in the form of a letter of concern follows the death and inquest of the former Manchester United and England footballer Nobby Stiles Stiles died in October 2020. His health had significantly deteriorated in the years prior to his death. He had become immobile and bed bound prior to his death due to his profound neurological disability Examination of his brain following his death confirmed an in life diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease In addition, he was found to have high stage chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), stage 3 Limbic-predominant age related TPD-43 encephalopathy (LATE) and small vessel cerebrovascular disease. All of which contributed to his death The CTE was caused by the requirement to repeatedly head a football throughout his time playing football

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester, said being chosen for the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme, which supports aspiring lawyers from under-represented backgrounds, had given her the confidence to "reach my goals" and "opened doors" The bursary is a tribute to 18-year-old Anthony, who had ambitions to study law but was murdered in a racist attack on Merseyside in 2005 Uche said she had been inspired by his family's fight for justice and wanted to draw on Anthony's own values when building her career Anthony's mother, Dr Gee Walker, set up a foundation in her son's name to tackle racism, hate crime and discrimination In partnership with the CPS and the National Black Crown Prosecution Association, the foundation offers an Anthony Walker Bursary - as well as a mentor - to help aspiring lawyers from under-represented Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds in the north-west of England It aims to help "remove barriers" for people, give financial support and opportunities for experience

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rhamero West was murdered in Old Trafford, Manchester, in September 2021 after a car chase in the city. evidence_packet.lead: The infant, named Ava by Greater Manchester Police, was discovered by a dog walker near Ashtons Field, in Little Hulton, Salford, on 20 November 2024 Despite a long-running investigation and a £50,000 reward put up by the Greater Manchester combined authority, detectives have sti
evidence_packet.summary: The infant, named Ava by Greater Manchester Police, was discovered by a dog walker near Ashtons Field, in Little Hulton, Salford, on 20 November 2024 Despite a long-running investigation and a £50,000 reward put up by the Greater Manchester combined authority, detectives have sti
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The infant, named Ava by Greater Manchester Police, was discovered by a dog walker near Ashtons Field, in Little Hulton, Salford, on 20 November 2024 Despite a long-running investigation and a £50,000 reward put up by the Greater Manchester combined authority, detectives have still not been able to identify the child's mother Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said its determination to find the answers "has never wavered", and that it wanted to "secure the justice that Ava deserves" Det Insp Louise Kelly said: "We know 20 November will be particularly significant for Ava's parents, family members, and anyone who may have known her." She added: "Behind every line of enquiry, every review of evidence, and every piece of information we assess is a baby girl who will never be forgotten." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton’s providing new forms of support for residents struggling with the cost of living, as presented at Bolton’s Tackling Poverty networking event held at Bolton Albert Halls on November 12 The cost of living is a major concern for many, and it may get tougher during the winter, as such, the event and the targeted support offered to people across Bolton offer some reassurance to those worst affected The support spans a large number of areas including helping access emergency food, heating, and financial assistance The event brings those organisations providing support together so they can better understand what is available across the town and as such can make informed decisions about who to refer people to for the most appropriate help In total there were over 40 organisations attending the event including the public, voluntary, and community sector, and other parters who were highlighting their services all were encouraged to network, share information, and create a more connected and efficient framework The presentations highlighted how Bolton’s Tacking Poverty Strategy can make a real difference, and how the Crisis, and Resilience Fund is being allocated to help groups across the borough

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Jo Platt MP with GM Blood Bikes Chair Russ Harrison, Leader of Wigan Council Cllr Nazia Rehman, and Wigan Council representatives Wigan Council has become one of the first local authorities in Greater Manchester to formally allow Blood Bikes to use bus lanes while carrying out their vital duties The council has amended its bus lane Traffic Regulation Order (TRO) to allow Blood Bike riders on official duties to legally use bus lanes across the borough, helping to ease the journey of volunteers and reduce the risk of unnecessary delays A volunteer-led charity, Greater Manchester Blood Bikes transport blood, plasma, vaccines, breast milk, emergency medicine and more to hospitals and healthcare settings all year round Leader of Wigan Council, Councillor Nazia Rehman, said: “I am incredibly proud that we are leading the way to give Blood Bikes riders access to bus lanes while carrying out their vital duties “These volunteers provide an invaluable service to our communities and NHS, and this decision is a practical way of recognising their dedication and commitment

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC LIVE Updated 12 mins ago Man United transfer news LIVE: Mauricio Pochettino eyes £84m target as contract talks begin Mauricio Pochettino's reign at Manchester United has begun in the worst possible way and the January transfer window cannot com Winter is most definitely here and whilst it may be freezing, new United boss Mauricio Pochettino is already feeling the heat. His first game at the helm against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday was a tall order - but the 4-0 battering prolonged the glum mood hanging around Old Tra Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card condemned Pochettino's men to defeat and it wasn't just the Frenchman who caught flak for his performance. A handful of other first-team stars, including fellow defender Matthijs de Ligt, were torn to shreds Pochettino will want to swiftly put this loss behind him and with January just around the corner, hope is likely resting on a productive winter window Rumours are already starting to fly regarding who the Argentine will want to recruit, so stick with us at the Manchester Evening News as we bring you all the latest updates throughout the day! Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Mon “He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.” The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence. Grealish, however, had struggled to replicate last season’s form impact when joining He added: “Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, more goals. There’s lots of things about him which we need and he’s good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap».
